text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE oncall — kv-cache TP shards reporting high queue depth, NCCL stalls, and a large spike in 5xxs. Alert summary: kv-cache.tp_shard_* queue_len > 2000 on multiple shards, continuous-batcher flush rate abnormal. (root_ts=1843217777)

raj: I'm on it. Seeing a p99 jump on generation paths — baseline ~120ms -> ~1.2s. Error rate up ~12% 5xx. Logs show repeated NCCL WARN/ERROR followed by cache eviction thrash.

jun: quick paste from runtime logs:
```
[2026-06-12T14:02:03Z] WARN nccl: NCCL WARN: AllGather stalled, peer timeout, rank=2 size=8
[2026-06-12T14:02:04Z] ERROR kv-cache: shard=3 queue_len=2124 continuous_batcher.flush_rate=6.2/s kv_size=8.3GB
[2026-06-12T14:02:04Z] ERROR kv-cache: slow-encode key=prefix_abcd evict_attempts=5
```

raj: initial hypothesis — last night's rollout lowered continuous_batching.max_wait_ms from 10->2ms to reduce latency; effect was more aggressive micro-batching. That increased number of small KV entries across requests, leading to uneven KV partition sizes across TP shards. When some peers had little data the NCCL all-gather patterns caused stalls (imbalance + live re-shard thrash).

marta: customer-impact notes: confirmed sustained 504s for org-acme and org-42-prod between 14:00-14:20 UTC. CS opened 3 tickets; one enterprise reported timeouts in production.

jun: mitigation plan options:
- OPTION A: flip feature-flag to disable continuous batching globally (fast).
- OPTION B: revert the max_wait_ms change to previous value (needs rollout, slower).
- OPTION C: force re-shard / rebalance KV and restart TP workers to clear NCCL states.
- OPTION D: scale up pod count temporarily to reduce queue depth.

raj: doing a combination: apply hotfix (OPTION A) to stop ongoing blowup, then rolling restart TP kv workers (OPTION C) to clear NCCL; follow with controlled revert of the config if stable. Executing now:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/kv-cache CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false --record
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/kv-cache-tp
```

ops-bot: :gear: env update applied to deploy/kv-cache (CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false).
ops-bot: :rocket: rollout restart started for deploy/kv-cache-tp (5 pods).

raj: observing logs while restarts proceed. After pod-2 restart, NCCL warnings dropped significantly on that shard. p50/p95 improved already.

jun: metric snapshot ~5m post-toggle:
- error_rate(5xx) down 85% vs peak
- p99 latency dropped from 1.2s -> ~230ms
- queue_len median back to normal range (~200)
One shard still shows slightly elevated KV size; scheduling rebalance job next.

raj: starting controlled rebalance: setting control-plane flag `kv_rebalance=true` and triggering reshard endpoint. Command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/kv/reshard?policy=balanced
```

ops-bot: reshard job queued (job_id=reshard-184321).

marta: customer update: Acme confirmed improvements, latency restored on their traffic. CS will notify remaining affected customers; will draft a status update.

maya: I'm taking the handoff at 14:40 UTC. I'll own monitoring and follow-ups. Key next actions for oncall:
- watch NCCL error alerts for next 2 hours
- verify no regressions in throughput due to disabling continuous batching
- validate reshard job completed and shard sizes equalized
- open postmortem and link back to rollout that changed max_wait_ms

raj: handing over to maya. Created follow-up INF ticket INF-3456 to revert the config change, add a unit/integration test that simulates uneven prefix distributions, and add an alert on KV-shard imbalance before NCCL thresholds.

marta: created customer-facing note draft; will sync with comms.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (monitoring). Severity: Sev2. Actions: hotfix disable continuous batching, restart TP kv workers, reshard. Owner: maya (oncall).

maya: will monitor and run extra checks. If anything reappears I'll escalate and execute revert (OPTION B). :thumbsup:

raj: TL;DR — rollout made batching too aggressive -> KV partition blowups -> uneven TP shard sizes -> NCCL stalls -> latency/errors. Hotfix disables continuous batching and restarts workers; reshard and revert planned. Postmortem to follow.
